As a former Amazon driver, I can attest that these working conditions are not only accurate, they're commonplace. I still remember my last day, cause the route they gave me was absolute BS.

I'm in a small ahh dodge Amazon van with 16 bags and 54 overflow packages.  Most of the overflow was big too, and taking up so much space that I couldn't even walk around the back of the van. The only spots that had space were the front seat and the passenger seat that was soon to be full too if I had worked. 

The fault lies with Amazon and these garbage DSPs who use scumbag tactics like rescues to keep you from getting your 10 hours a day.  

I will NEVER go back to that company. Amazon can burn to the ground for their employee abuse. Whole signs in the cafeteria encouraging people not to unionize is actually evil.
